title: Bekhorot 33
description: Beit Hillel’s case that non-priests, menstruating women and even gentiles may eat a blemished firstborn; why one may not skin a firstborn or a disqualified consecrated animal whole from its feet; and the dispute over letting the blood of a firstborn congested with blood, set beside a barrel of teruma whose purity is in doubt.

a1.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל: הָנֵי מִילֵּי תָּם, אֲבָל בַּעַל מוּם כְּתִיב ״הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יַחְדָּיו יֹאכְלֶנּוּ״, וּמָה טָמֵא שֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים אוֹכֵל בִּבְכוֹר, זָר שֶׁאוֹכֵל בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיֹּאכַל בִּבְכוֹר.

a2.he: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְטָמֵא, שֶׁכֵּן הוּתַּר מִכְּלָלוֹ בַּעֲבוֹדַת צִבּוּר!

a3.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל, אַטּוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה קָאָמַר? בַּאֲכִילָה קָאָמְרִינַן, אֲכִילַת זָר עֲדִיף.

a4.he: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַתִּיר, וַאֲפִילּוּ גּוֹי. מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא? ״כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל״ — מָה צְבִי וְאַיָּל מוּתָּר לְגוֹי, אַף פְּסוּלִין מוּתָּר לְגוֹי.

a5.he: וְאִידַּךְ? תְּלָתָא ״צְבִי וְאַיָּל״ כְּתִיבִי, חַד לְכִדְרַבִּי יִצְחָק, וְחַד לְכִדְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא, וְחַד לְכִדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר.

a6.he: וְאִידַּךְ? מָה צְבִי וְאַיָּל פְּטוּרִים מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה, אַף פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין פְּטוּרִין מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה.

a7.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּכוֹר אֵין מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ לְנִדּוֹת, דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ לְנִדּוֹת. מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי? דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָךְ״, מָה הָתָם נִדּוֹת לָא, אַף הָכָא נִדּוֹת לָא.

a8.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל: הָנֵי מִילֵּי תָּם, אֲבָל בַּעַל מוּם — ״הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יֹאכְלֶנּוּ״.

a9.he: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי, הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּאֵין טוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ, אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּטוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ — לָא.

a10.he: דְּאַשְׁכְּחַן דְּפַלֵּיג רַחֲמָנָא בֵּין טוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ, לְבֵין שֶׁאֵין טוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ, דִּתְנַן: הַפֶּסַח שֶׁבָּא בְּטוּמְאָה — לֹא יֹאכְלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ זָבִים וּמְצוֹרָעִין וְזָבוֹת וְנִדּוֹת וְיוֹלְדוֹת.

a11.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל: הָתָם הוּא דְּגַלִּי רַחֲמָנָא ״טְמֵא נֶפֶשׁ״, אֲבָל הָכָא ״טָמֵא״ סְתָמָא כְּתִיב, לָא שְׁנָא.

a12.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מַרְגִּילִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב, כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ אֵין מַרְגִּילִין בַּבְּכוֹר, וְלֹא בִּפְסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין.

a13.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא יוֹם טוֹב — דְּקָא טָרַח טִירְחָא דְּלָא חֲזֵי לֵיהּ. אֶלָּא בְּכוֹר — מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא, דְּאָמַר אֵין מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ לְנִדּוֹת.

a14.he: וְלֹא בִּפְסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין. מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, דִּתְנַן: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי חַטָּאוֹת, אַחַת תְּמִימָה וְאַחַת בַּעֲלַת מוּם — תְּמִימָה תִּקְרַב, בַּעֲלַת מוּם תִּיפָּדֶה.

a15.he: נִשְׁחֲטָה בַּעֲלַת מוּם, אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִזְרַק דָּמָהּ שֶׁל תְּמִימָה — מוּתֶּרֶת, אִם מִשֶּׁנִּזְרַק דָּמָהּ שֶׁל תְּמִימָה — אֲסוּרָה.

a16.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בָּשָׂר בִּקְדֵירָה, וְנִזְרַק דָּמָהּ שֶׁל תְּמִימָה — אֲסוּרָה.

a17.he: וְרַב חִסְדָּא, לוֹקְמַהּ כּוּלַּהּ כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי! דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אֶלָּא בִּבְכוֹר, דִּקְדוּשָּׁתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם, אֲבָל פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין דְּאֵין קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם — לָא.

b1.he: וְלוֹקְמַהּ כּוּלַּהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן! דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָתָם אֶלָּא פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין, דְּאַלִּימִי לְמִיתְפַּס פִּדְיוֹנוֹ, אֲבָל בְּכוֹר דְּלָא אַלִּים לְמִיתְפַּס פִּדְיוֹנוֹ — לָא.

b2.he: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵית לֵיהּ כׇּל פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין נִמְכָּרִין בָּאִיטְלִיז וְנִשְׁקָלִין בְּלִיטְרָא? אַלְמָא דְּכֵיוָן דְּאִיכָּא רַוְוחָא לְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שָׁרֵי לֵהּ!

b3.he: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא: מַה שֶּׁמַּשְׁבִּיחַ בָּעוֹר — פּוֹגֵם בַּבָּשָׂר. בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא אָמְרִי: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה בְּקָדָשִׁים.

b4.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין אוֹמֵר: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יְגַדֵּל מֵהֶן עֲדָרִים עֲדָרִים.

b5.he: מַתְנִי׳ בְּכוֹר שֶׁאֲחָזוֹ דָּם, אֲפִילּוּ מֵת — אֵין מַקִּיזִין לוֹ דָּם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יַקִּיז, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֶׂה בּוֹ מוּם, וְאִם עָשָׂה בּוֹ מוּם — הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִשְׁחַט עָלָיו. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: יַקִּיז, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה בּוֹ מוּם.

b6.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּכוֹר שֶׁאֲחָזוֹ דָּם — מַקִּיזִין לוֹ אֶת הַדָּם בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂים בּוֹ מוּם, וְאֵין מַקִּיזִין לוֹ אֶת הַדָּם בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשִׂין בּוֹ מוּם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.

b7.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אַף בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה בּוֹ מוּם, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁחַט עַל אוֹתוֹ הַמּוּם. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף נִשְׁחָט עַל אוֹתוֹ הַמּוּם. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ מֵת — אֵין מַקִּיזִין לוֹ אֶת הַדָּם.

b8.he: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לִבְרֵיהּ, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא לִבְרֵיהּ: כַּמַּחְלוֹקֶת כָּאן, כָּךְ מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּחָבִית שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, דִּתְנַן: חָבִית שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד בָּהּ סְפֵק טוּמְאָה — רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיְתָה בִּמְקוֹם הַתּוּרְפָּה — יַנִּיחֶנָּה בְּמָקוֹם הַמּוּצְנָע, אִם הָיְתָה מְגוּלָּה — יְכַסֶּנָּה.

b9.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיְתָה מוּנַּחַת בְּמָקוֹם הַמּוּצְנָע — יַנִּיחֶנָּה בִּמְקוֹם הַתּוּרְפָּה, אִם הָיְתָה מְכוּסָּה — יְגַלֶּנָּה. רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: לֹא יְחַדֵּשׁ בָּהּ דָּבָר.

b10.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְרַבָּנַן כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.

b11.he: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם, דְּקָא עָבֵיד בְּיָדַיִם, אֲבָל הָכָא דִּגְרָמָא — כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ!

b12.he: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם, אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּא יָבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ וִיטַהֲרֶנָּה, אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּאִי שָׁבֵיק לֵיהּ מָיֵית — כְּרַבָּנַן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ!

b13.he: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָכָא, דְּאִי שָׁבֵיק לֵיהּ מָיֵית, אֲבָל הָתָם — שֶׁמָּא יָבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ וִיטַהֲרֶנָּה, כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סְבִירָא לְהוּ! וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָכָא, דְּקָא עָבֵיד בְּיָדַיִם, אֲבָל הָתָם דִּגְרָמָא — כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ!

b14.he: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם, דְּשֶׁמָּא יָבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ וִיטַהֲרֶנָּה, אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּאִי שָׁבֵיק לֵיהּ מָיֵית, כְּרַבָּנַן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ!

b15.he: וְעוֹד, הָכָא בִּקְרָאֵי פְּלִיגִי וְהָכָא בִּקְרָאֵי פְּלִיגִי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בִּמְחַמֵּץ אַחַר מְחַמֵּץ שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב, דִּכְתִיב ״לֹא תֵאָפֶה חָמֵץ״ וְ״לֹא תֵעָשֶׂה״.

b16.he: בִּמְסָרֵס אַחֵר מְסָרֵס שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב, דִּכְתִיב: ״וּמָעוּךְ וְכָתוּת וְנָתוּק וְכָרוּת״, אִם עַל כּוֹרֵת חַיָּיב, עַל נוֹתֵק לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן? אֶלָּא לְהָבִיא נוֹתֵק אַחַר כּוֹרֵת, שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב.

b17.he: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּמֵטִיל מוּם בְּבַעַל מוּם, דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: ״כׇּל מוּם לֹא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ״, וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: ״תָּמִים יִהְיֶה לְרָצוֹן״.

b18.he: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הַאי ״תָּמִים יִהְיֶה לְרָצוֹן״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ? מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמַעוֹטֵי בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ.

b19.he: בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ — פְּשִׁיטָא, דִּיקְלָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא!

b20.he: אֶלָּא לְמַעוֹטֵי פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וַאֲסִירִי בְּגִיזָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה — בְּמוּמִין נָמֵי לִיתַּסְרוּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b21.he: וְרַבָּנַן נָמֵי, הָכְתִיב ״כׇּל מוּם לֹא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ״! לִגְרָמָא הוּא דְּאָתֵי, דְּתַנְיָא: ״מוּם לֹא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ״ — אֵין לִי

messages.text: Continued from 32b: a baraita taught that Beit Shammai let only priests partake of a blemished firstborn, since “their flesh shall be yours, as the wave breast and the right thigh”; Beit Hillel permit non-priests, and according to Rabbi Akiva even gentiles.

And Beit Hillel would respond to that claim: This statement applies only to an unblemished firstborn offering, which is sacrificed upon the altar. But concerning a blemished firstborn it is written: “You shall eat it within your gates; the impure and the pure may eat it alike.”

verse.he: בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יַחְדָּו כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל׃
verse.en: Eat it in your settlements, the impure among you no less than the pure, just like the gazelle and the deer.

notes.he: איתקש לחזה ושוק דהא קרא בתם קמשתעי דכתיב לעיל מיניה את דמם תזרוק אבל בעל מום כתיב בפרשת כל הבכור (דברים ט״ו:כ״ב) הטמא והטהור יחדו:
notes.en: This applies only to an unblemished firstborn: [only it] is juxtaposed to the breast and thigh, since that verse speaks of an unblemished one, as is written just before it: “You shall sprinkle their blood.” But concerning a blemished one it is written, in the passage “Every firstborn” (Deuteronomy 15:22): “The impure and the pure alike.”

notes.he: אף על גב דהאי קרא מיירי נמי בבעל מום בין לרב בין לדבי רב דלעיל בריש עד כמה (בכורות דף כח.) ובין לרבי ישמעאל בין לרבי עקיבא דפ' איזהו מקומן בסופו (זבחים דף נז.) ובין לרבי ישמעאל ובין לרבי יוסי הגלילי דבריש ב"ש (זבחים דף לז.) אבשרם דמשמע אחד תם ואחד בעל מום או מיהיה (לו) דדריש לימד על הבכור בעל מום שנותנו לכהן מ"מ אתי קל וחומר ומפיק מהיקשא ונאכל לזרים מאחר דמתוקמא היקשא דכחזה התנופה בתם ובכי האי גונא אשכחן בפ"ק דזבחים (דף י:) גבי אשם שנכנס דמו פסול לא מצית אמרת קל וחומר מעולה אף על גב דרבנן אית להו היקישא דחטאת כאשם למלתא אחריתי כדמוכח סוגיא התם ובפ"ק דקדושין (דף יד.) אתי קל וחומר ומפקא מגזירה שוה בגמרא ובמיתת היבם גבי וכל היכא דכתיב (חוקה) [עיכובא] לא דרשינן ק"ו ובשמעתין דמצות עשה שהזמן גרמא גבי טפלים חייבין נשים לא כל שכן והא דלקמן דריש פ' ט' (דף נג:) דדרשינן מהיקשא דעשר תעשר מקיש בהמה למעשר דגן מה מעשר דגן מן החדש על הישן לא ומפקא מק"ו דכבשים ועזים שהם כלאים זה בזה מתעשרים מזה על זה חדש וישן כו' התם לא מיתוקמא היקשא אי אתית למידן ק"ו ואע"ג דלרבי יוסי בר' יהודה צריכי היקשא לכדאמר בההוא פירקא דמה מעשר ניטל באומד ובמחשבה וכו' וצריכא נמי לכדדרשי' בזבחים בסוף פ' בית שמאי (זבחים דף מה.) קדשי עובדי כוכבים אין חייבין מ"מ עיקר אתיא היקש לשנה שנה והא דבכל הבשר (חולין דף קטז.) איכא מ"ד דבשר בחלב אסור באכילה ומותר בהנאה מגזירה שוה דקדש קדש ואיכא למאן דאסר אף בהנאה מק"ו לא קשיא מידי אההיא דקדושין (דף נו) כדפרשינן בקדושין:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot note that the verse “and their flesh shall be yours” also speaks of a blemished firstborn: so it is for both Rav and the school of Rav at the beginning of chapter 4 (28a), for both Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva at the end of Eizehu Mekoman (Zevaḥim 57a), and for both Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili at the beginning of Beit Shammai (Zevaḥim 37a), who expound “their flesh” to mean both unblemished and blemished, or expound “shall be [yours]” to teach that a blemished firstborn is given to the priest. Even so, Beit Hillel’s a fortiori inference comes and removes [the blemished firstborn] from the juxtaposition, so that non-priests may eat it, since the juxtaposition “as the wave breast” can still be applied to the unblemished one. They cite parallels where an a fortiori inference overrides a juxtaposition or a verbal analogy: Zevaḥim 10b, on a guilt offering whose blood entered [the Sanctuary], although the Rabbis use the juxtaposition of sin offering to guilt offering for another matter; Kiddushin 14a, on the death of the yavam, and the rule that wherever indispensability is written no a fortiori inference is expounded; and the passage on positive time-bound mitzvot (“the little ones are obligated; women, all the more so”). The passage in chapter 9 (53b), where the juxtaposition of animal tithe to grain tithe (not tithing new for old) overrides the a fortiori inference from sheep and goats, is different: there the juxtaposition would be left without application if one followed the a fortiori inference, for although Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda needs it for other teachings (tithe taken by estimation and by thought; and gentiles’ consecrated items, Zevaḥim 45a), its main purpose is “year by year.” Nor is Ḥullin 116a, where meat in milk is permitted for benefit by a verbal analogy and prohibited even for benefit by an a fortiori inference, a difficulty for Kiddushin (56b), as they explained in Kiddushin. notes.he: דכתיב הטמא והטהור יאכלנו:
notes.en: Eats of a firstborn: as it is written, “The impure and the pure shall eat it.”

messages.text: Beit Hillel derive an a fortiori inference: And if a ritually impure priest, who may not eat the meat of offerings of lesser sanctity, nevertheless may eat the meat of a blemished firstborn offering, then with regard to a non-priest, who may eat the meat of offerings of lesser sanctity, e.g., peace offerings and animal tithe offerings, is it not logical that he may eat the meat of a blemished firstborn offering?

notes.he: שלמים ומעשר ופסח:
notes.en: A non-priest, who eats offerings of lesser sanctity: peace offerings, [animal] tithe and the Paschal offering.

messages.text: This a fortiori inference can be refuted: What is notable about the case of a ritually impure priest? It is notable in that its general prohibition was permitted in certain circumstances, specifically with regard to the communal service. If there are no ritually pure priests, the sacrificial service may be performed by ritually impure priests. By contrast, it is never permitted for a non-priest to perform the sacrificial service. Accordingly, one cannot derive the halakha concerning a non-priest via an a fortiori inference from an impure priest.

notes.he: דאם אין כהן טהור באותו בית אב עושה טמא עבודת צבור דכתיב במועדו ואפילו בשבת ואפי' בטומאה:
notes.en: In the communal service: if there is no pure priest in that ancestral house [on duty], an impure one performs the communal service, as it is written “in its appointed time”: even on Shabbat and even in impurity.

notes.he: איכא למיפרך מה לכהן טמא דין הוא שאוכל בכור שכן הותר מכללו בעבודת ציבור כדכתיב במועדו ואפי' בטומאה:
notes.en: This can be refuted: what of an impure priest? It is reasonable that he eats of a firstborn, since he was permitted out of his general [prohibition] in the communal service, as it is written “in its appointed time”: even in impurity.

messages.text: And Beit Hillel would respond: Is that to say that the a fortiori inference was stated with regard to the sacrificial service, which was the subject of that refutation? Not so; rather, we state it with regard to the eating of sacrificial meat, and the eating of a non-priest is superior to that of a ritually impure priest. Accordingly, the refutation of the a fortiori inference is inapplicable.

notes.he: קמיירי ובאכילה זר עדיף מטמא כדאמרן בקדשים קלים דלא משכחת אכילה דכהן טמא מותר בה וזר אסור בה:
notes.en: [The inference] speaks of a non-priest’s eating, and in eating a non-priest is superior to an impure [priest], as we said with offerings of lesser sanctity; for you cannot find any eating that is permitted to an impure priest and forbidden to a non-priest.

notes.he: ואכילת זר בקדשים קלים זר עדיף למיכלינהו טפי מכהן טמא והלכך ב"ה מתירין. מה צבי ואיל מותר להאכיל העובד כוכבים עמו אף בכור נמי:
notes.en: We are speaking of eating: and as for eating offerings of lesser sanctity, a non-priest is better placed to eat them than an impure priest; therefore Beit Hillel permit. [And Rabbi Akiva:] just as with a gazelle and a deer one may feed a gentile together with him, so too with a firstborn.

messages.text: § The baraita stated that according to Rabbi Akiva, Beit Hillel deems it permitted for non-priests, and even gentiles, to partake of blemished firstborn offerings. What is the reason of Rabbi Akiva?

The verse states: “Like the gazelle and like the deer.” Just as a gazelle and a deer are permitted to be eaten by a gentile, so too, disqualified blemished firstborn offerings are permitted to be eaten by a gentile.

verse.he: בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יַחְדָּו כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל׃
verse.en: Eat it in your settlements, the impure among you no less than the pure, just like the gazelle and the deer.

messages.text: And the other one, i.e., the tanna who disagrees with Rabbi Akiva’s version of the opinion of Beit Hillel, who does not deem it permitted for a gentile to partake of a blemished firstborn offering, what is his reason?

The terms “gazelle” and “hart” are written three times in the context of disqualified consecrated animals, in Deuteronomy 12:15, 12:22, and 15:22. One is required for the statement of Rabbi Yitzḥak and Rabbi Oshaya, and one is needed for the statement of Rabbi Elazar HaKappar.

notes.he: תנא קמא אליבא דבית הלל אמר לך תלתא צבי ואיל כתיבי בראה אנכי חד לכדרבי יצחק ורבי אושעיא ולא נתפרש לנו היכן:
notes.en: And the other: the first tanna, according to Beit Hillel, would tell you: “gazelle and deer” are written three times in [the portion] “See, I [set before you]”: one for the statement of Rabbi Yitzḥak and Rabbi Oshaya, and it has not been explained to us where [that statement is]. [Rashi, like the translation, reads a single statement of Rabbi Yitzḥak and Rabbi Oshaya; the Aramaic printed on the daf reads two.]

notes.he: בשחיטת חולין בפ' שני (דף כח.):
notes.en: For the statement of Rabbi Elazar HaKappar: in Shechitat Ḥullin, in the second chapter (28a).

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס דלא אתפרש ורבינו חננאל מפרש דהיינו ההיא דפ"ב דמכות (דף כב.) המרביע שור פסולי המוקדשין והמנהיג שור פסולי המוקדשין לוקה גוף אחד הן ועשאן הכתוב שני גופין פירוש שהשור בפני עצמו נחשב כצבי וכאיל דהיינו שני מינין ולא כמו שרגילין לפרש שם שקצת הוא כקדשים וקצת הוא כחולין אלא מצבי ואיל נפקא כדקאמר הכא:
notes.en: One for the statement of Rabbi Yitzḥak and Rabbi Oshaya: Rashi explained that it is not explained [where it is]. Rabbeinu Ḥananel explains that it is the one in the second chapter of Makkot (22a): one who mates an ox of disqualified consecrated animals [with another kind], or who drives an ox of disqualified consecrated animals [with another kind], is flogged; it is one body, and the verse made it two bodies. That is, the ox by itself is considered like a gazelle and a deer, which are two species; not as people usually explain there, that it is partly like consecrated items and partly like non-sacred. Rather it derives from “gazelle and deer,” as is said here.

notes.he: ת"ק סבר תלתא צבי ואיל כתיבי. רק בכל אות וגו' אך כאשר יאכל את הצבי ואת האיל בשעריך תאכלנו חד לכדר' יצחק אמר רבי אושעיא והא דר' יצחק אמ"ר אושעיא לא משתכחנא בכולה גמרא דידן. וחד לכדר' אלעזר הקפר כדאמר בשחיטת חולין רבי אלעזר הקפר אומר מת"ל אך כאשר יאכל את הצבי ואת האיל וגו' מקיש צבי ואיל לבהמה מה בהמה בשחיטה אף צבי ואיל בשחיטה:
notes.en: And the other: the first tanna holds that “gazelle and deer” is written three times: “Only with all the desire [of your soul]” etc. [Deuteronomy 12:15]; “Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten” [12:22]; “Within your gates you shall eat it” [15:22]. One for the statement that Rabbi Yitzḥak said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya, and this statement of Rabbi Yitzḥak in the name of Rabbi Oshaya I cannot find in all of our Gemara. And one for the statement of Rabbi Elazar HaKappar, as it says in Shechitat Ḥullin: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar says: What does the verse teach with “Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten” etc.? It juxtaposes the gazelle and deer to a domesticated animal: just as a domesticated animal [requires] slaughter, so a gazelle and a deer [require] slaughter.

messages.text: The Aramaic printed here reads “one for Rabbi Yitzḥak, and one for Rabbi Oshaya, and one for Rabbi Elazar HaKappar.” The translation, Rashi and Rabbeinu Gershom read a single teaching of Rabbi Yitzḥak and Rabbi Oshaya (Rabbeinu Gershom: Rabbi Yitzḥak in the name of Rabbi Oshaya), which Rashi says he cannot locate.

And the other verse teaches that just as a gazelle and a deer are exempt from the first of their offspring being counted a firstborn, as the verse states: “All the firstling males that are born of your herd and of your flock,” referring specifically to domesticated animals but not undomesticated animals such as a gazelle and a deer; so too, disqualified consecrated animals are exempt from the first of their offspring being counted a firstborn (see 14a).

verse.he: כׇּל־הַבְּכוֹר אֲשֶׁר יִוָּלֵד בִּבְקָרְךָ וּבְצֹאנְךָ הַזָּכָר תַּקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ וְלֹא תָגֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנֶךָ׃
verse.en: You shall consecrate to the ETERNAL your God all male firstlings that are born in your herd and in your flock: you must not work your firstling ox or shear your firstling sheep.

messages.text: One may not give a blemished firstborn offering to menstruating women to eat; this is the statement of Beit Shammai. And Beit Hillel say: One may give it to menstruating women to eat.

notes.he: ה"ה לבעל קרי דלא שרו רק לטומאה שהותרה בפסח כדמוכח בסמוך:
notes.en: One may not give it to menstruating women to eat: the same applies to one who had a seminal emission, for [Beit Shammai] permit only the impurity that was permitted with the Paschal offering, as is evident shortly.

messages.text: What is the reason of Beit Shammai? It is written with regard to the firstborn offering: “And their flesh shall be yours, as the wave breast and the right thigh.” Just as there, with regard to the wave breast and the right thigh, menstruating women may not eat them, as these consecrated meats may not be eaten by a ritually impure individual, so too here, with regard to the firstborn offering, menstruating women may not eat its meat, as it too is consecrated.
messages.quote: One may not give a blemished firstborn offering to menstruating women to eat

verse.he: וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה־לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וּכְשׁוֹק הַיָּמִין לְךָ יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: But their meat shall be yours: it shall be yours like the breast of elevation offering and like the right thigh.

notes.he: חזה ושוק נדות לא דטמא שאכל את הקדש חייב בכרת:
notes.en: Just as there: the breast and thigh, menstruating women may not [eat them], since an impure person who eats consecrated food is liable to karet.

messages.text: And Beit Hillel would respond: This statement, i.e., this verse, is referring only to the meat of an unblemished firstborn offering. Only such meat is compared to the wave breast and the right thigh. But with regard to a blemished firstborn offering, the verse explicitly states that the impure and the pure may eat it (see Deuteronomy 15:22).

And Beit Shammai would claim: This statement, that the ritually impure may eat the meat of a blemished firstborn offering, applies only where the impurity does not issue upon him from his own body but is contracted from an external source, e.g., from a corpse or the carcass of a creeping animal. But where the impurity issues upon him from his own body, such as in the case of a zav or a menstruating woman, that individual may not eat the meat of a blemished firstborn offering.

Beit Shammai continue: This is a valid distinction, as we find that the Merciful One distinguishes between a case where the impurity issues upon an individual from his own body and between a case where the impurity does not issue upon him from his own body.

When the Paschal offering is sacrificed in a state of ritual impurity, due to the fact that the majority of the Jewish people are ritually impure, then zavim and lepers and zavot and menstruating women and women after childbirth may not eat from it.

notes.he: שנטמאו רוב צבור במת ועשו פסח בטומאה לא יאכלו ממנו זבים וזבות אע"ג דאכלי ליה טמאי מתים. אלמא שני לן בין טומאה היוצאה מגופו לטומאה שאינה יוצאה מגופו:
notes.en: The Paschal offering that comes in impurity: when most of the community became impure through a corpse and they performed the Paschal offering in impurity, zavim and zavot may not eat of it, even though those impure through a corpse do eat it. Evidently we do distinguish between impurity that issues from his body and impurity that does not issue from his body.

messages.text: The sacrificing of the Paschal offering overrides only ritual impurity imparted by a corpse; it does not override other forms of ritual impurity.

And Beit Hillel would respond: It is only there, in the case of the Paschal offering, that a difference of that kind applies, as the Merciful One revealed that only an individual whose impurity did not issue from his own body is permitted to eat the Paschal offering, as the verse states: “Impure by reason of a dead body.”

verse.he: דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי־יִהְיֶה־טָמֵא ׀ לָנֶפֶשׁ אוֹ בְדֶרֶךְ רְחֹקָהׄ לָכֶם אוֹ לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם וְעָשָׂה פֶסַח לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: Speak to the Israelite people, saying: Regarding anyone—whether you or your posterity—who is defiled by a corpse or is on a long journey and would offer a passover sacrifice to GOD:

notes.he: דזבין לא יאכלו משום דבהדיא גלי רחמנא טמא נפש מותרין ותו לא דכתיב (במדבר ט׳:י׳) איש כי יהיה טמא לנפש וגו' ומינה דייקינן איש נדחה לפסח שני ולא צבור ובטמא נפש הוא דגלי רחמנא איש ולא צבור אבל טומאת זבות כדקיימי קיימי אבל הכא בבכור סתמא כתב רחמנא הטמא והטהור:
notes.en: It is there: that zavim may not eat, because the Merciful One revealed explicitly that those impure through a corpse are permitted, and no others, as it is written (Numbers 9:10): “If any man shall be impure by reason of a dead body” etc. From it we infer: an individual is deferred to the second Pesaḥ, but not the community. So it was concerning one impure through a corpse that the Merciful One revealed “a man” and not the community, but the impurity of zavim stays as it was. But here, with a firstborn, the Merciful One wrote without qualification: “the impure and the pure.”

messages.text: But here, with regard to the firstborn offering, the term “impure” is written unspecified: “The impure and the pure may eat it alike.” Therefore, in this case there is no difference between the two types of impurity.

notes.he: לנשי כהנים נדות ונדה טומאה יוצאה עליה מגופה. התם דגלי רחמנא טמא נפש למעוטי טומאה יוצאה מגופו:
notes.en: To menstruating women: to priests’ wives who are menstruating, and a menstruating woman’s impurity issues upon her from her body. There, the Merciful One revealed “impure by reason of a dead body,” to exclude impurity that issues from his body.

messages.text: One may not skin an animal from its feet [margilin] on a Festival. Although it is permitted to slaughter and skin an animal on a Festival, one may not skin it in such a manner that he will retain the hide intact to function as a vessel. Similarly, one may not skin a firstborn offering from its feet, even on a weekday and even if it is blemished, nor is skinning by way of the feet permitted in the case of disqualified consecrated animals.

notes.he: ואפי' בעל מום להפשיטו דרך הרגלים כל העור שלם לעשות ממנו מפוח לנפחים או למוכרי דבש ושמן שנותנין אותו בעורות כבשים המפשיטין שלימים:
notes.en: One may not skin a firstborn from its feet: even a blemished one, stripping it by way of the legs with the whole hide intact, to make a bellows from it for smiths, or for sellers of honey and oil, who put [their wares] in sheepskins stripped whole.

notes.he: אע"פ שנפדו ושחטן לאכילה:
notes.en: Nor disqualified consecrated animals: even though they were redeemed and he slaughtered them for eating.

notes.he: אין מרגילין אין מפשיטין עור בהמה שלם דרך רגל לצורך מפוח:
notes.en: One may not skin from the feet: one may not strip an animal’s hide whole by way of the leg, for [use as] a bellows.

messages.text: Such an act is considered degrading to the animal, even if the animal has been redeemed and slaughtered.

Granted, one may not skin an animal from its feet on a Festival, as one is thereby performing an effort whose outcome is not needed for use on the Festival. But with regard to a firstborn offering, who is the tanna who taught that skinning it from its feet is prohibited?
messages.quote: Similarly, one may not skin a firstborn offering from its feet

notes.he: ביום טוב:
notes.en: Which is not needed for him: on the Festival.

notes.he: לצורך י"ט ולא בבכור ובפסולי המוקדשין משום בזיון:
notes.en: An effort that is not needed: for the Festival. And not with a firstborn and with disqualified consecrated animals, because of degradation.

messages.text: It is the opinion of Beit Shammai, who say that one may not feed the meat of a firstborn offering to menstruating women.

notes.he: דסברי בכור בעל מום בקדושתו קאי אפי' לאחר שחיטה כתם וכי היכי דתם אין מרגילין משום בזיון דקדשים דפוגם הבשר דמתיירא לחתוך העור וחותך הבשר בבעל מום נמי אין מרגילין:
notes.en: It is Beit Shammai: who hold that a blemished firstborn remains in its sanctity, even after slaughter, like an unblemished one. And just as with an unblemished one one may not skin from the feet, because of the degradation of consecrated items, since it damages the meat (being wary of cutting the hide, he cuts the meat), so too with a blemished one one may not skin from the feet.

notes.he: ב"ש דאמר אין מאכילין אותו לנדות כלומר כי היכי דמחמרי ביה בהא מחמיר נמי באחרינא דאין מרגילין:
notes.en: Beit Shammai, who say one may not give it to menstruating women to eat: that is, just as they are stringent with it in this, so they are stringent in another matter too, that one may not skin it from its feet.

messages.text: According to Beit Shammai, a blemished firstborn retains its sanctity as though it were unblemished, and must be treated in the manner of sacrificial meat. Skinning an animal from its feet is considered an act inappropriate for such meat and is therefore prohibited.
The Gemara analyzes the next clause of the baraita: Nor is skinning by way of the feet permitted in the case of disqualified consecrated animals. Who is the tanna who taught this?
messages.quote: nor is skinning by way of the feet permitted in the case of disqualified consecrated animals

messages.text: It is Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, as we learned in a baraita:

notes.he: דמחמיר בפסולי המוקדשין דאמר אפילו לאחר שחיטה בקדושתייהו קיימי:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon: who is stringent with disqualified consecrated animals, saying that even after slaughter they remain in their sanctity.

messages.text: One had before him two sin offerings that he consecrated to achieve atonement for his sin so that in the event that one of them was lost or died the other would effect atonement. One of them was unblemished and the other one became blemished after having been consecrated. The halakha is that the unblemished offering should be sacrificed, whereas the blemished one should be redeemed.

notes.he: שהפרישן לאחריות שאם תאבד האחת יתכפר בחבירתה ונפל מום באחת:
notes.en: Two sin offerings: which he set aside as a guarantee, so that if one is lost he will gain atonement with the other; and a blemish befell one of them.

notes.he: לחטאתו:
notes.en: The unblemished one shall be sacrificed: as his sin offering.

notes.he: ודמיה לנדבת שופרות:
notes.en: The blemished one shall be redeemed: and its money goes to the chests for voluntary offerings.

notes.dh: דתניא היו לפניו שתי חטאות כו'
notes.he: ברייתא בתמורה בפ' ולד חטאת (דף כד.) ומיירי כשהפריש שתי חטאות לאחריות והרי עתה אחת תמימה ואחת בעלת מום שבמשנה [קרבה שניה עד] שלא נשחטה ראשונה תמות שכבר כפרו בעליה ויש לתמוה דבברייתא אסרי רבנן בעלת מום כשנשחטה לאחר זריקת דם של תמימה ובמשנה שרי ורבי אלעזר בר' שמעון אסר בברייתא בכל ענין ובמשנה שרי כשנשחטה קודם לכן ואומר ר' דבמשנה מיירי שהפריש פרה בעלת מום וחיללה על התמימה שכל קדושה של בעלת מום נכנסה בתמימה ותפסה קדושתה ולכך מותרת הבעלת מום לרבנן בכל ענין דלא דמיא לחטאת שכיפרו בעליה ורבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון מחלק בין נשחטה קודם זריקה לנשחטה לאחר זריקה אבל הכא מיירי שהתמימה באה ע"י קדושת עצמה ולא חילל הבעלת מום עליה כי אם על דמים ואין נראה כאילו פקע קדושה שלה כיון דאין התמימה באה מכחה הלכך לרבנן נזרק דמה לפני שחיטה הבעלת מום אסורה דדמיא לחטאת שכפרו בעליה ולרבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון אסורה בכל ענין דדמיא לחטאת שכפרו בעליה:
notes.en: As it is taught: He had before him two sin offerings, etc.: This baraita is in Temura, chapter Velad Ḥattat (24a), and it deals with one who set aside two sin offerings as a guarantee, and now one is unblemished and one blemished; while in the mishna [there: if the second was sacrificed] before the first was slaughtered, [the first] must die, since its owners have already achieved atonement. One may wonder: in the baraita the Rabbis prohibit the blemished one when it was slaughtered after the sprinkling of the unblemished one’s blood, yet in the mishna it is permitted; and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon prohibits it in every case in the baraita, yet in the mishna he permits it when it was slaughtered beforehand. My teacher says: the mishna deals with one who set aside a blemished animal and transferred [its sanctity] onto the unblemished one, so that all the sanctity of the blemished one entered the unblemished one, which took on its sanctity. Therefore, according to the Rabbis the blemished one is permitted in every case, since it is not like a sin offering whose owners achieved atonement, and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon distinguishes between where it was slaughtered before the sprinkling and after it. But here the case is that the unblemished one comes by virtue of its own sanctity, and he did not transfer the blemished one onto it but onto money, so it does not appear that its sanctity lapsed, since the unblemished one does not come by its power. Therefore, according to the Rabbis, if [the unblemished one’s] blood was sprinkled before the blemished one was slaughtered, the blemished one is prohibited, since it is like a sin offering whose owners achieved atonement; and according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon it is prohibited in every case, since it is like a sin offering whose owners achieved atonement.

notes.he: כגון שהפריש ב' חטאות לאחריות שאם תאבד אחת או (תפיל) [תפול] בה מום שתהא שניה תחתיה:
notes.en: One unblemished and one blemished: for example, where he set aside two sin offerings as a guarantee, so that if one is lost or a blemish befalls it, the second will be in its place.

messages.text: If the blemished animal was redeemed and slaughtered before the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled on the altar to effect the atonement, the blemished animal is permitted to be eaten. But if the blemished one was slaughtered after the blood of the unblemished animal was already sprinkled upon the altar, the blemished animal is prohibited both in consumption and benefit.

notes.he: אחר פדיונה:
notes.en: The blemished one was slaughtered: after its redemption.

notes.dh: אם עד שלא נזרק דמה של תמימה
notes.he: נשחטה:
notes.en: If before the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled: it was slaughtered,

notes.he: באכילה ואע"ג שנזרק דם התמימה קודם שתיאכל בשר בעלת מום דסבירא לן דמאחר שבאת לכלל היתר זביחה שוב אין בה קדושה בבעלת מום:
notes.en: Permitted: to be eaten, even though the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled before the meat of the blemished one was eaten, since we hold that once it came to be permitted through slaughter, the blemished one no longer has any sanctity.

notes.he: נשחטה אסורה אפילו בהנאה דהויא לה חטאת שכיפרו בעליה ולמיתה אזלא דזו היא אחת מחמש חטאות מתות:
notes.en: If after the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled: it was slaughtered, it is prohibited even for benefit, for it is a sin offering whose owners have achieved atonement, which is left to die; this is one of the five sin offerings that are left to die.

notes.he: נשחטה הבעלת מום אסורה דהויא חטאת שכיפרו בעליה דלמיתה אזלא:
notes.en: If after the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled: the blemished one was slaughtered, it is prohibited, for it is a sin offering whose owners achieved atonement, which is left to die.

messages.text: Since its owner’s atonement is effected by the sprinkling of the blood of the unblemished offering on the altar, at this stage the blemished animal must be put to death, in accordance with the halakha that a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement with another sin offering must die.

Even if the blemished animal was slaughtered and its meat is being cooked in the pot, and only then was the blood of the unblemished animal sprinkled on the altar, the meat of the blemished animal is still prohibited.

notes.he: בשר בעלת מום דסבירא ליה אפילו לאחר שחיטה בקדושתייהו קיימי וחטאת שכיפרו בעליה מיקריא:
notes.en: Even meat in the pot … is prohibited: the meat of the blemished one, since he holds that even after slaughter they remain in their sanctity, and it is called a sin offering whose owners achieved atonement.

notes.dh: רבי אלעזר בן שמעון אומר אפי' בשר בעלת מום בקדירה
notes.he: כלומר אע"ג דנשחטה קודם שנזרק דמה ואע"ג דבשר בקדירה דהוי כמבושל כיון שלא נאכל אלא לאחר זריקה אסור. וכי היכי דמחמיר הכא בהך בעלת מום דהויא פסולי המוקדשין הם הכי מחמיר דאין מרגילין בפסולי המוקדשין:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Shimon says: Even the meat of the blemished one in the pot: that is, even though it was slaughtered before [the unblemished one’s] blood was sprinkled, and even though the meat is in the pot, as good as cooked, since it was not eaten until after the sprinkling it is prohibited. And just as he is stringent here with this blemished one, which counts among disqualified consecrated animals, so he is stringent that one may not skin disqualified consecrated animals from their feet.

messages.text: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, maintains that disqualified blemished offerings retain a measure of their sanctity even after being slaughtered. Since the blemished sin offering was not yet eaten when the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled, it is considered a sin offering whose owner has achieved atonement, and therefore it is prohibited for one to derive benefit from it. The opinion of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, accords with the ruling of the baraita with regard to skinning a disqualified consecrated animal from its feet.
But let Rav Ḥisda establish the entire baraita in accordance with the opinion of Beit Shammai.

notes.he: דקס"ד דכי היכי דמחמרי ב"ש בבכור מחמרי נמי בשאר פסולי המוקדשין:
notes.en: Let him establish all of it in accordance with Beit Shammai: for it entered our mind that just as Beit Shammai are stringent with a firstborn, they are also stringent with other disqualified consecrated animals.

messages.text: Perhaps Beit Shammai say that the sanctity of a blemished offering is retained only in the case of a firstborn offering, as its sanctity is from the womb. But with regard to a disqualified consecrated animal, whose sanctity is not from the womb, perhaps they do not maintain that its sanctity remains even after it has been slaughtered. It is therefore necessary to attribute the latter clause of the baraita to Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon.
But if so, let Rav Ḥisda establish the entire baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon.

Perhaps Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says that the sanctity of a slaughtered blemished offering is retained only there, with regard to other disqualified consecrated animals, because their level of sanctity is strong enough to transfer their sanctity to their redemption money. But with regard to a blemished firstborn offering, whose level of sanctity is not strong enough to transfer it to its redemption money, perhaps its sanctity is not retained, and therefore one may skin the hide from its feet.

notes.he: דאילימי למיתפס פדיונן דבני פדייה נינהו אבל בכור אין קדושתו חמורה כ"כ שיהא תופס פדיונו ה"נ (כשהיא) כשמרגילין בפסולי המוקדשים דאיכא רווחא להקדש שהעור נמכר ביוקר לצורך מפוח לישרי ליה:
notes.en: Which are strong enough to transfer [sanctity to] their redemption: since they are subject to redemption. But a firstborn’s sanctity is not so severe that it transfers to its redemption. So too, when one skins disqualified consecrated animals from their feet there is a benefit to the Temple, since the hide sells dearly for a bellows; let it be permitted to him.

messages.text: But doesn’t Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, agree with the ruling of the mishna (31a) that all disqualified consecrated animals are sold in the butchers’ market and weighed and sold by the litra, in the manner of non-sacred meat? Certainly he agrees with that halakha. Evidently, since there is a benefit that accrues to the Temple treasury, the tanna of the mishna deems this permitted.

notes.he: דמחמיר בפסולי המוקדשין לאחר שחיטה מי לית ליה הא דתנן נמכרין באיטליז אלמא לאו בקדושתייהו קיימי ומשום האי רווחא דהקדש דכיון דזימנין דטפי ופריק מעיקרא כדאמרן שרי ליה מר ה"נ לישרי להרגיל משום רווחא דהקדש דכיון דימכור העור ביוקר טפי ופריק מעיקרא:
notes.en: And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon: who is stringent with disqualified consecrated animals after slaughter: does he not hold what we learned, that they are sold in the butchers’ market? Evidently they do not remain in their sanctity, and because of this benefit to the Temple, since at times he will pay more when he redeems it at the outset, as we said, the Master permitted it. So too, let him permit skinning from the feet because of the benefit to the Temple: since he will sell the hide at a higher price, he will pay more when he redeems it at the outset.

messages.text: As it was taught (31b), the meat of disqualified consecrated animals may be treated in this manner despite the fact that it retains a measure of sanctity. The reason is that if the owner knows that it is permitted for him to perform this more lucrative action, he is likely to spend more money to redeem the animal in the first place, which benefits the Temple treasury. By the same logic, why doesn’t Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, permit the more lucrative action of skinning the animal from its feet?

The benefit gained to the hide by skinning it whole is offset by the detriment caused to the flesh. Part of the animal’s flesh is severed from the carcass during the skinning process, thereby lowering its value.
messages.quote: since there is a benefit that accrues to the Temple treasury

notes.he: וליכא רווחא בבשר כולי האי שהרי מחתך את הבשר ופושטה עם העור:
notes.en: Damages the meat: so there is not that much benefit, because of the meat, since he cuts into the meat and strips it off with the hide.

notes.he: ל"א לא הוי רווחא להקדש דמה שמשביח בעור פוגם בבשר שמחתכו ומנוולו כעובד עבודה בקדשים מפוח:
notes.en: [ל״א, another version:] There is no benefit to the Temple, since what improves the hide damages the meat, for he cuts it and spoils it. Like one performing work with consecrated animals [an editor’s note: it seems it should read “since he prepares the hide for a bellows while it is still on the consecrated animal”]. Bellows.

messages.text: Skinning a disqualified consecrated animal from its feet is prohibited because it appears as though he is performing work with sacrificial animals, which is prohibited.
messages.lead: In the West, Eretz Yisrael, they say in the name of Ravina:

notes.he: לעיל קאי. כלומר לעולם דברי הכל היא דאסור להרגיל דבזיון גדול הוא שנראה כעובד עבודה בקדשים שמוכרין העור לצורך מפוח כשהוא עדיין על הקדשים:
notes.en: In the West they say: this refers back to above. That is, in fact it is everyone’s opinion that skinning from the feet is prohibited, since it is a great degradation, for he appears to be performing work with consecrated animals, as they sell the hide for a bellows while it is still on the consecrated animal.

messages.text: This prohibition is a rabbinic decree, lest one retain the disqualified consecrated animals in his possession while waiting for a consumer to purchase the hides, and in the meantime raise many herds of disqualified animals from them. In such a case, he might shear or work the animals in a prohibited manner.

notes.he: כלומר דברי הכל אסור להרגיל דאי שרית ליה אתי לשהוייה מלשחוט עד שימצא בני אדם המבקשים עורות שלימים ובין כך ובין כך יגדל עדרים מפסולי המוקדשין ואתי בהו לידי תקלה לגיזה ועבודה:
notes.en: Lest he raise herds upon herds: that is, all agree that skinning from the feet is prohibited, for if you permit it to him he will come to delay slaughtering until he finds people who want whole hides, and meanwhile he will raise herds of disqualified consecrated animals and come to a stumbling with them in shearing and labor.

notes.he: שמא אין שם נפחים מי שצריכין להן והוא משהן בחיים עד שיזדמנו שם והוא מגדל מהן עדרים עדרים קודם שיבאו הנפחים ואתי בהו לידי תקלה לגיזה ועבודה:
notes.en: A decree, if you permit skinning from the feet: perhaps there are no smiths there who need them, and he will keep them alive until [such buyers] turn up there, and he will raise herds upon herds of them before the smiths come, and come to a stumbling with them in shearing and labor.

messages.text: Mishna

With regard to a firstborn animal that was congested with excess blood, even if the animal will die if one does not let the excess blood, one may not let its blood, as this might cause a blemish, and it is prohibited to cause a blemish on consecrated animals. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: אפינדו"ר:
notes.en: Mishna. That was congested with blood: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: אם לא יקיזוהו:
notes.en: Even if it will die: if they do not let its blood.

notes.he: ואפי' במקום שאין עושין מום דיכול לחזור ולהתרפאות המכה והכי מפרש בפ"ק דפסחים מתוך שאדם בהול על ממונו אי שרית ליה במקום שאין עושה בו מום אתי למיעבד במקום שעושה בו מום:
notes.en: One may not let its blood: even in a place where it does not make a blemish, where the wound can heal again. And so it is explained in the first chapter of Pesaḥim: since a person is anxious about his money, if you permit him in a place where it makes no blemish, he will come to do it in a place where it makes a blemish.

notes.he: נזקק במאי פליגי:
notes.en: A firstborn that was congested with blood, etc.: [The printed Tosafot here consists only of the words:] one must look into what they disagree about.

notes.dh: אפי' מת אין מקיזין לו את הדם
notes.he: דאי שרית ליה במקום שאין עושה בו מום. שמא יקיז אפי' במקום שעושה מום:
notes.en: Even if it will die, one may not let its blood: for if you permit him in a place where it causes no blemish, perhaps he will let blood even in a place where it causes a blemish.

messages.text: One may let the blood provided that he will not cause a blemish while doing so, and if he caused a blemish, the animal may not be slaughtered on account of that blemish. Since he was the cause of the blemish, he may not slaughter the animal until it develops a different, unrelated blemish.

notes.he: שלא יחתוך ושלא יפגום את אזנו ואת ניב שפתיו שאין עתיד לחזור ולהתרפאות דסברי רבנן כ"ש אי לא שרית ליה במקום שאין עושה מום אתי למיעבד במקום מום:
notes.en: He may let blood, provided that he does not cause a blemish: that he does not cut or damage its ear or the rim of its lip, which will not heal again. For the Rabbis hold: all the more so, if you do not permit him in a place where it makes no blemish, he will come to do it in a place of a blemish.

notes.he: במום הזה הואיל והטילו עד שיפול בו מום אחר:
notes.en: He may not slaughter on its account: on account of this blemish, since he inflicted it, until another blemish befalls it.

notes.dh: אם עשה בו מום הרי זה לא ישחט עליו
notes.he: דקנסינן ליה:
notes.en: If he caused a blemish in it, he may not slaughter on its account: for we penalize him.

messages.text: One may let the blood even if he thereby causes a blemish in the animal.

notes.he: דסבר ר"ש דבר שאין מתכוין מותר:
notes.en: He may let blood even in a place where it makes a blemish: for Rabbi Shimon holds that an unintended act is permitted.

notes.he: ר' שמעון אומר יקיז אפי' שעושה בו מום דדבר שאין מתכוין מותר:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says: He may let blood even where he causes a blemish in it, since an unintended act is permitted.

messages.text: Gemara

With regard to a firstborn animal that was congested with excess blood, and which can be healed only through bloodletting, one may let the animal’s blood by cutting it in a place where the incision does not cause a permanent blemish. But one may not let the animal’s blood by cutting it in a place where the incision causes a permanent blemish, as it is prohibited to intentionally cause a blemish in a firstborn animal; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

One may even let the animal’s blood by cutting it in a place where the incision causes a permanent blemish, provided that he does not slaughter the animal on the basis of that blemish, even though in general, a firstborn animal may be slaughtered once it develops any permanent blemish.

notes.dh: גמ' וחכ"א יקיז אף במקום שעושה מום
notes.he: אם צריך להקיז מאותו אבר ולא יניחנו שימות:
notes.en: Gemara. And the Rabbis say: he may let blood even in a place that makes a blemish: if he needs to let blood from that limb; he should not leave it to die.

messages.text: The animal may even be slaughtered on the basis of that blemish.
Even if the firstborn would die if its blood is not let, one may not let its blood at all.
Just as there is a dispute here in this baraita with regard to bloodletting, so there is a dispute in a mishna with regard to a barrel of teruma.
messages.lead: The Gemara relates: Rabbi Elazar taught his son, and some say it was Rabbi Ḥiyya who taught his son:

messages.text: In the case of a barrel of teruma oil with regard to which uncertainty developed concerning its status of ritual impurity, and which therefore may not be eaten,

notes.he: שנמצא שרץ בצידה. וספק נגע ספק לא נגע:
notes.en: With regard to which uncertainty developed: a creeping animal was found beside it, and it is uncertain whether it touched it or did not touch it.

messages.text: One must nevertheless safeguard the teruma from impurity. Therefore, if the barrel was resting in a vulnerable location, where it might come into contact with impurity, one should place it in a concealed location, and if it was exposed, he should cover it.

notes.he: במקום גילוי ואינו משומר:
notes.en: Vulnerable location: an exposed place, not guarded.

notes.he: מקום מגולה:
notes.en: A vulnerable location: an exposed place.

notes.he: שלא יגע בה טומאה דשמא יבא אליהו ויטהרנה:
notes.en: He should place it in a concealed location: so that impurity will not touch it, for perhaps Elijah will come and declare it pure.

messages.text: That is not necessary. Rather, if it was placed in a concealed location, one may place it in a vulnerable location. If it was covered he may expose it, as he need no longer safeguard this teruma from impurity.

notes.he: מעכשיו אינה ראויה לאכילה שמא טמאה היא ולא לזילוף שמא טהורה ואסור לאבדה הלכך יגלנה ותיטמא ותהא ראויה לזילוף:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says, etc.: from now on it is not fit for eating, since perhaps it is impure, nor for sprinkling [as impure teruma may be used], since perhaps it is pure; and one may not destroy it. Therefore he exposes it so that it becomes impure and will be fit for sprinkling.

notes.dh: ור' יהושע סבר כיון דספק היא מותר לגרום לה טומאה
notes.he: להסיקה תחת תבשילו:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehoshua holds that since it is uncertain, one may cause it to become impure: [so as] to burn it under his cooking.

messages.text: One should do nothing new with it, i.e., he should leave the barrel as it is.

notes.he: לא יזיזנה ממקומו:
notes.en: He should do nothing new with it: he should not move it from its place.

messages.text: Rabbi Meir, who deems it permitted to let the firstborn offering’s blood provided that one does not cause a blemish, holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, who deems it prohibited to place the barrel in an exposed location lest it become ritually impure, which is equivalent to a blemish.

notes.he: דאוסר לקלקלו ומתיר לתקנו אם יכול לעשותו בלא מום קאמר דיקיז שלא ימות כר"א דאסור לגרום לה טומאה אלא מצניעה שלא תיטמא:
notes.en: Rabbi Meir: who forbids spoiling it and permits repairing it if he can do so without a blemish, saying he may let blood so that it will not die, holds like Rabbi Eliezer, who forbids causing it impurity and [says] he hides it so that it does not become impure.

messages.text: And the Rabbis, who deem bloodletting permitted even if it will cause a blemish, hold in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua, who rules that the contents of the barrel may be exposed to ritual impurity. And Rabbi Yehuda, who says that bloodletting is not permitted under any circumstance, holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Gamliel, who rules that the barrel should be left as is and not be handled at all.

notes.he: דשרו להטיל מום קודם שימות כדי שיראה לאכילה כר' יהושע דאמר יגרום לה טומאה כדי שיראה לזילוף ור' יהודה דאמר אע"ג דמית ואזיל לאיבוד לא יקלקלנו ולא יתקננו כר"ג דאמר לא יתקננה ולא יקלקלנה:
notes.en: And the Rabbis: who permit inflicting a blemish before it dies, so that it will be fit for eating, hold like Rabbi Yehoshua, who says one may cause it impurity so that it will be fit for sprinkling. And Rabbi Yehuda, who says that even though it is dying and going to waste one should neither spoil it nor repair it, holds like Rabban Gamliel, who says one should neither repair it nor spoil it.

messages.caption: The bloodletting dispute matched, opinion by opinion, to the dispute over the barrel of teruma, a match the Gemara goes on to reject.

messages.text: From where can one prove that these comparisons are accurate? Perhaps Rabbi Meir states his opinion, that one may not let blood in a place that will cause a blemish, only there, as the individual is causing the blemish by direct action. But here, in the case of the barrel, where the ritual impurity results from an indirect action, perhaps he holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua.
messages.quote: But one may not let the animal’s blood by cutting it in a place where the incision causes a permanent blemish

notes.he: שמטיל בו מום הלכך ימות מעצמו ולא יטיל בו מום:
notes.en: As he acts by direct action: inflicting a blemish on it; therefore it should die on its own and he should not inflict a blemish on it.

notes.he: בעלמא שמניחה במקום התורפה וגורם לה טומאה:
notes.en: Indirect: merely, in that he places it in the vulnerable place and causes it impurity.

notes.he: דמתיר שיגרום לה טומאה ותהא ראויה לזלף משיניחנה ולא תהא ראויה לכלום:
notes.en: He holds like Rabbi Yehoshua: who permits causing it impurity so that it will be fit for sprinkling, rather than leaving it fit for nothing.

notes.he: ע"כ לא קאמר רבי מאיר הכא דאין מקיזין לו במקום שעושה בו מום משום דקא עביד בידים:
notes.en: Rabbi Meir says here that one may not let its blood in a place that causes a blemish only because he acts by direct action.

messages.text: And furthermore, perhaps Rabbi Eliezer states his opinion that the barrel should be protected only here, because perhaps Elijah will come and deem it ritually pure. But there, with regard to the firstborn offering, where if one leaves the animal it will certainly die, perhaps he holds in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, that bloodletting is permitted in order to prevent the animal’s death.
messages.quote: should place it in a concealed location, and if it was exposed, he should cover it

notes.he: ויאמר שלא נגעה בה טומאה:
notes.en: Only lest Elijah come: and say that no impurity touched it.

messages.text: And likewise, perhaps the Rabbis state their opinion only here, with regard to the firstborn offering, as if one leaves it, the animal will certainly die. But there, in the case of the barrel of teruma, perhaps they accept the claim that one must safeguard the teruma, because perhaps Elijah will come and deem it ritually pure, which would mean that they hold in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer.
messages.quote: One may even let the animal’s blood by cutting it in a place where the incision causes a permanent blemish

messages.text: It can also be suggested that Rabbi Yehuda states his opinion, that bloodletting is prohibited in all circumstances, only here, with regard to the firstborn offering, as the individual is causing the blemish by direct action. But there, in the case of the barrel, where the ritual impurity results from an indirect action, perhaps he holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua.
messages.quote: one may not let its blood at all

messages.text: And perhaps Rabban Gamliel states his opinion, that the barrel should not be moved at all, only there, because perhaps Elijah will come and deem it ritually pure. But here, with regard to the firstborn offering, where if one leaves it, it will certainly die, it is possible that he holds in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis.
messages.quote: should do nothing new with it

messages.text: And furthermore, one cannot draw parallels between the opinions of the two sources, as here the tanna’im disagree with regard to the exposition of certain verses, and there they disagree with regard to the exposition of certain other verses.

All of the Sages who disagree as to whether one may let the blood of the firstborn animal concede that one who leavens a meal offering after another had already leavened it is liable to receive lashes for the additional leavening, as it is written: “It shall not be baked with leaven,” and it is also stated: “No meal offering that you sacrifice to God shall be made with leaven.” This indicates that one is liable for every act of leavening performed on a meal offering.
messages.lead: As Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

verse.he: לֹא תֵאָפֶה חָמֵץ חֶלְקָם נָתַתִּי אֹתָהּ מֵאִשָּׁי קֹדֶשׁ קׇדָשִׁים הִוא כַּחַטָּאת וְכָאָשָׁם׃
verse.en: It shall not be baked with leaven; I have given it as their portion from My offerings by fire; it is most holy, like the purgation offering and the reparation offering.

notes.he: רבנן נמי אע"ג דפליגי בבכור שאחזו דם דלא הוי המקיז דם מטיל מום בבעל מום דאין לך בעל מום גדול הימנו שהרי ימות כולהו מודו במנחות שהמחמץ אחר מחמץ כגון אם לש האחד בחימוץ ואפאה אחר שניהם חייבין דכתיב (ויקרא ו׳:י׳) לא תאפה חמץ ולא תעשה חמץ (שם ב) ודרשינן במנחות (דף נה:) אפייה בכלל בל תעשה חמץ למה יצאת מה אפייה מיוחדת שהיא מעשה יחידי וחייבין עליה בפני עצמה אף כל מעשה יחידי:
notes.en: All concede: the Rabbis too, even though they disagree about a firstborn congested with blood, [where] one who lets blood is inflicting a blemish on a blemished animal, for you have no blemished animal greater than this, since it will die [the printed text reads “is not inflicting”; the sense, as stated below, is that this is a blemish in a blemished animal]: all of them concede regarding meal offerings that one who leavens after one who leavens, for example, where one kneaded it with leaven and another baked it, both are liable, as it is written (Leviticus 6:10): “It shall not be baked with leaven,” and “shall not be made leavened” (Leviticus 2:11). And we expound in Menaḥot (55b): baking was included in “shall not be made leavened”; why was it singled out? Just as baking is distinct in being a single act and one is liable for it on its own, so too for every single act.

notes.he: היינו אופה אחר מחמץ שבאפייה מיגמרא מילתא דחמץ:
notes.en: One who leavens after one who leavens: that is, one who bakes after one who leavens, for with baking the leavening is completed.

messages.text: Similarly, everyone agrees that one who castrates an animal after one who has already castrated it is liable, as it is written: “Those whose testicles are bruised or crushed or detached or cut shall not be offered to the Lord, and you shall not do this in your land.”

verse.he: וּמָעוּךְ וְכָתוּת וְנָתוּק וְכָרוּת לֹא תַקְרִיבוּ לַיהֹוָה וּבְאַרְצְכֶם לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ׃
verse.en: You shall not offer to GOD anything [with its testes] bruised or crushed or torn or cut. You shall have no such practices in your own land,

notes.he: בבהמת חולין נמי אם כרת האחד הביצים ועדיין הם בכיס ובא חבירו ונתקן מן הכיס והשליכן שניהם חייבין:
notes.en: One who castrates after one who castrates: even with a non-sacred animal; if one cut the testicles while they were still in the scrotum, and his fellow came, detached them from the scrotum and threw them away, both are liable.

notes.he: דכתיב בתריה ובארצכם לא תעשו:
notes.en: If one is liable for cutting: as is written after it, “and in your land you shall not do [this].”

notes.he: מי שנותק אחר כורת:
notes.en: And one who castrates after one who castrates: one who detaches after one who cuts.

messages.text: If one is liable when the seminal vesicles are cut, then when the testicles are detached altogether, is he not all the more so liable? Rather, this verse serves to include one who detaches the testicles after one who cuts the seminal vesicles, to indicate that he is liable. Apparently, one is liable for castrating an animal that is already sterilized.

notes.he: שנותקו ומשליכו לא כל שכן:
notes.en: For detaching: detaching them and throwing them away, not all the more so?

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס דאם כרת האחד את הביצים ועדיין הם בכיס ובא חבירו ונתקן מן הכיס והשליכן שניהם חייבים וקשיא לרבי דלקמן בפרק על אלו מומין (בכורות דף לט:) משמע דנתוק וכרות איתנהו לביצים בסוף גמרא דחוטין החיצוניות שנפגמו דקאמר נתוק וכרות לא הוי מומין דהא איתנהו ובההיא שמעתא פי' רש"י נתוק ביד לגמרי אלא שעדיין תלוין בכיס כרות בסכין ועדיין תלוין בכיס ומעורין קצת דכרות הוי בציר מנתוק כדאמר בפירקין דלעיל להביא נותק אחר כורת עכ"ל:
notes.en: To include one who detaches after one who cuts: Rashi explained that if one cut the testicles while they were still in the scrotum, and his fellow came, detached them from the scrotum and threw them away, both are liable. My teacher finds this difficult, for below in chapter Al Elu Mumin (39b) it implies that with detached and cut testicles they are still there: at the end of the Gemara on the outer threads that were damaged, where it says that detached and cut are not blemishes, since they are still there. And in that passage Rashi explained: detached, by hand, completely, but still hanging in the scrotum; cut, with a knife, still hanging in the scrotum and slightly attached; for cut is less than detached, as it says in our chapter above: “to include one who detaches after one who cuts.” End of quotation.

notes.he: מי שכורת הכיס ומניח הביצים תלוין. על נותק הביצים לא כ"ש:
notes.en: If one is liable for cutting: one who cuts the scrotum and leaves the testicles hanging; for detaching the testicles, not all the more so?

messages.text: These Sages disagree only with regard to one who causes a blemish in an already blemished animal, such as one whose blood circulation is constricted.

notes.he: כגון האי בכור שאחזו דם:
notes.en: In a blemished animal: such as this firstborn congested with blood.

messages.text: As Rabbi Meir maintains that as the verse states: “It shall be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it,” this categorical statement includes even the causing of a blemish in an offering that is already blemished.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יַקְרִיב זֶבַח־שְׁלָמִים לַיהֹוָה לְפַלֵּא־נֶדֶר אוֹ לִנְדָבָה בַּבָּקָר אוֹ בַצֹּאן תָּמִים יִהְיֶה לְרָצוֹן כׇּל־מוּם לֹא יִהְיֶה־בּוֹ׃
verse.en: And when anyone offers, from the herd or the flock, a sacrifice of well-being to GOD for an explicit uncertain. vow or as a freewill offering, it must, to be acceptable, be without blemish; there must be no defect in it.

notes.he: וקרי ביה לא יהיה בו שלא יטיל מום ומדהוה ליה למיכתב מום וכתיב כל מום לרבות אפילו בעל מום שלא יטיל בו מום אחר:
notes.en: “There shall be no blemish in it”: read it as “there shall be no [blemish put] in it,” that one may not inflict a blemish. And since it could have written “blemish” and wrote “any blemish,” it includes even a blemished animal, that one may not inflict another blemish in it.

notes.dh: דר' מאיר סבר כל מום לא יהיה בו
notes.he: בין בתם בין בבעל מום אסור לעשות בו מום ורבנן סברי תמים יהיה לרצון כל מום לא יהיה בו כלומר דבתם אסור להטיל מום ולא בבעל מום. והאי שאחזו דם כבעל מום דמי:
notes.en: For Rabbi Meir holds “There shall be no blemish in it”: whether unblemished or blemished, it is prohibited to make a blemish in it. And the Rabbis hold “It shall be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it”: that is, in an unblemished one it is prohibited to inflict a blemish, but not in a blemished one. And this one congested with blood is like a blemished one.

messages.text: And the Rabbis maintain that the phrase “It shall be perfect to be accepted” indicates that the prohibition against causing a blemish applies only to an animal that is currently perfect, i.e., unblemished, and can therefore be accepted, i.e., it is fit to be sacrificed upon the altar. If the animal is already blemished, there is no prohibition against causing an additional blemish in it.

notes.he: דרשינן כוליה קרא תמים יהיה לרצון כל מום לא יהיה בו דמשמע תמים הראוי לרצון אמרתי לך דכל מום לא תטיל בו אבל בעל מום לא ורבי יהודה סבר כר"מ ומיהו גזר מקום שאין עושין בו מום אטו מקום שעושין בו מום:
notes.en: And the Rabbis hold: we expound the whole verse, “It shall be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it,” which implies: [of] a perfect animal, fit to be accepted, I told you that you shall inflict no blemish in it, but not a blemished one. And Rabbi Yehuda holds like Rabbi Meir, but he decreed against a place where they make no blemish because of a place where they do make a blemish.

messages.text: And Rabbi Meir, what does he do with this verse: “It shall be perfect to be accepted”?
messages.quote: It shall be perfect to be accepted

messages.text: That verse serves to exclude only an animal that was blemished from the outset, i.e., an animal that was born with a blemish. In such a case, there is no prohibition against causing an additional blemish in it. But if the animal was initially unblemished and later developed a blemish, it is prohibited to cause another blemish in it.

notes.he: קודם שהקדישה היה בו מום:
notes.en: From the outset: before he consecrated it, it had a blemish.

notes.he: ורבי מאיר ההוא תמים יהיה כל מום לא יהיה בו למעוטי בעל מום מעיקרו ממעי אמו דמותר להטיל מום ולא באחוז דם. במומין נמי ליתסרו להטיל בהן מום קמ"ל תמים יהיה לרצון:
notes.en: And the other: and Rabbi Meir, [uses] “It shall be perfect … there shall be no blemish in it” to exclude an animal blemished from the outset, from its mother’s womb, in which it is permitted to inflict a blemish, but not one congested with blood. [And as for] “let them also be prohibited to inflict blemishes in them,” it teaches us [with] “It shall be perfect to be accepted.”

messages.text: There is no need to exclude an animal that was blemished from the outset, as it is merely like a palm tree, i.e., it can never attain the status of an animal consecrated as an offering. Therefore, it is obvious that the prohibition against causing a blemish does not apply to this animal.

notes.dh: בעל מום מעיקרו פשיטא דיקלא בעלמא הוא
notes.he: תימה לימא דלבכור איצטריך שיש בו קדושת הגוף ואין לו פדיון וי"ל דניחא לאשכוחי דאיצטריך לכל הקדשים דהכי נמי מצי למימר דאיצטריך לזמן הזה דלא עבר משום מטיל מום אפי' בתם ואפילו למאן דמחייב למטיל מום בבעל מום בזמן הזה גרע כדקאמר בפ"ק דע"ז (דף יג:) ולא לדמיה חזי אלא משכח שפיר דאיצטריך אפי' בזמן בית המקדש ומיהו אף על גב דפרישית דבזמן הזה גרע ממטיל מום בבעל מום אין לתמוה מהא דפסקינן לקמן הלכה כר"ש דברייתא דשרי להטיל מום בבעל מום והתם במס' ע"ז (גז"ש) אסר רבא לקדשים בזמן הזה לנשר פרסותיה משום דנראה כמטיל מום בקדשים דאע"ג דמטיל מום בבעל מום שרי מדאורייתא מ"מ מדרבנן מיהא אסור ולא שרינן הכא אלא משום הקזה:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot ask why the Gemara calls an animal blemished from the outset obvious, “a mere palm tree”; let it say that the verse was needed for a firstborn, which has bodily sanctity and no redemption. They answer that the Gemara prefers to find a need that covers all consecrated animals. It could likewise have said the verse was needed for the present day, when one does not transgress the prohibition of causing a blemish even in an unblemished animal, and even according to the one who holds one liable for causing a blemish in a blemished animal, since nowadays it is worse, as stated in the first chapter of Avoda Zara (13b), being not fit even for its value; but the Gemara rightly finds a need that applies even in Temple times. And although they explained that nowadays it is worse than causing a blemish in a blemished animal, one should not wonder at our ruling below, that the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon of the baraita, who permits causing a blemish in a blemished animal, while in Avoda Zara Rava forbade cutting off the hooves of consecrated animals nowadays because it looks like causing a blemish in consecrated animals: although causing a blemish in a blemished animal is permitted by Torah law, it is at least prohibited by rabbinic law, and here it was permitted only because of the bloodletting. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: Rather, Rabbi Meir maintains that the phrase “It shall be perfect to be accepted” serves to exclude disqualified consecrated animals, to teach that after their redemption, when they become non-sacred, the prohibition against causing a blemish does not apply to them any longer.

notes.he: להטיל בו מום:
notes.en: Let them also be prohibited with blemishes: [prohibited] to inflict a blemish in it.

messages.text: This exclusion is necessary, as it might enter your mind to say that since even after they have been redeemed and are non-sacred, just as it is prohibited to shear these animals or use them for labor, perhaps let it also be prohibited to cause a blemish upon them. Consequently, this verse teaches us that there is no prohibition against causing a blemish in these animals.

And as for the Rabbis as well, who derive their opinion from the verse: “It shall be perfect to be accepted,” isn’t it written: “There shall not be any blemish in it,” which indicates an expansion of the prohibition against causing a blemish upon an offering?

notes.he: הא כתיב כל מום לא יהיה בו דמשמע דאפי' בבעל מום לא:
notes.en: And the Rabbis: but it is written “There shall not be any blemish in it,” which implies: even in a blemished one, no.

messages.text: That verse comes to teach that the prohibition against causing a blemish extends also to a blemish caused as the result of an indirect action.

notes.he: ההוא לגרמא כתיב שלא יהיה בו:
notes.en: That is written for an indirect action: that there shall not be [a blemish] in it.

messages.text: The verse states: “There shall not be any blemish in it”; from here I have derived…

The baraita continues on 34a: …only that one may not cause a blemish directly; “any blemish” teaches that one may not cause one indirectly either, such as placing figs or dough on the animal’s ear so that a dog will come and bite it.
